title: Mux Pricing in 2026 Is Cheap Until Delivery Minutes Add Up
summary: Mux pricing has four plans with monthly fees as credits toward metered usage. Your bill depends on how many video delivery minutes you use.
body_markdown:
## Catching a Mux usage spike with Activepieces


Before a viewer spike turns into a surprise invoice, Activepieces, whose core is MIT-licensed, can watch your Mux usage on a schedule and warn you. It only reports the bill and never changes it.


If you keep a metered feature such as per-view analytics, the cost of that choice still moves with traffic, which is why the distinction matters after the last section. Nothing in the plan itself will tell you when it has moved too far.


One fact carries the mechanism: Mux exposes usage through its API, so the numbers behind your invoice can be fetched without opening the dashboard.


Running on a timer, the workflow below pulls the usage figures for encoding, storage and delivery, projects them to the end of the month, and then either pings a channel or appends a row to a sheet.


Trace the path in the diagram from trigger to branch: the eye icon marks it as observation only. No step touches your Mux configuration, so a bad estimate costs you a false alarm, not an outage.


### What the workflow checks and when it alerts


Start with the trigger: it's a schedule, and its frequency is your first real decision. Delivery is the line that grows with viewers, so a daily check catches a spike while it's still a small share of the month.


A weekly check can let one viral video run for days unseen.


After the usage fetch, the estimate step takes month-to-date totals and extrapolates them across the remaining days. Be aware of the limit of that arithmetic: a straight-line projection assumes the rest of the month looks like the days so far.


An early spike overstates the total and a late one understates it.


Set the branch threshold from your own model, ideally the point where the next plan becomes cheaper, and compare projected spend with it. Above it, the workflow posts to Slack.


Below it, the workflow writes a row to a sheet, which builds a record of how usage tracks against your forecast. That record is what lets you revise the model rather than guess again.


### Alternatives that need no extra tool


You don't need Activepieces for this, though cost isn't the reason to skip it: a daily check is about 30 runs a month against the free plan's 1,000 credits.


Mux's own dashboard alerts can notify you on usage thresholds, which suits a team that wants no extra moving parts, though you accept whatever conditions the dashboard offers.


If you already have cron, a scheduled script calling the same API does the identical job in a few lines. The trade-off is maintenance: a script has no visual run history, while a workflow tool gives you one and adds a service to host.
